steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Piaget proposed that children's thinking develops through four stages: sensorimotor (0-2), pre-operational (2-7), concrete operational (7-11), formal operational (11+). Each stage represents a qualitative change in thinking.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Schemas are mental frameworks that organise knowledge. Assimilation: fitting new information into existing schemas. Accommodation: modifying schemas when new information doesn't fit. Equilibration drives development - disequilibrium motivates accommodation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Conservation: understanding that quantity stays the same despite changes in appearance. Pre-operational children fail conservation tasks (e.g. pouring liquid into a taller, narrower glass). Concrete operational children succeed.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Egocentrism: pre-operational children struggle to see things from another's perspective. Piaget's Three Mountains Task showed children could not describe the view from a doll's position.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Assimilation = fitting INTO existing schema. Accommodation = CHANGING the schema. Pre-operational children CANNOT conserve. Concrete operational children CAN. Vygotsky emphasises SOCIAL interaction. Piaget emphasises INDIVIDUAL discovery.
